pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/114918

Allow EQL to execute queries also when some shards are unavailable.
This adds a new parameter (both available as a query parameter and in the request body) , `allow_partial_search_results` (default `false`, that can be configured as a cluster setting `xpack.eql.default_allow_partial_results`), that enables this behavior.

If shard failures happen during the query, the execution only takes into consideration the available shards, and returns an additional "shard_failures" value in the response

```
{
   "query": "sequence ...",
   "allow_partial_search_results": true
}
```

```
{
    "is_partial": false,
    "is_running": false,
    "took": ...,
    "timed_out": false,
    "hits": {
        ...
     },
    "shard_failures": [
        {
            "shard": ...,
            "index": ...,
            "node": ...,
            "reason": {
                "type": "no_shard_available_action_exception",
                "reason": null
            }
        }
    ]
}
```

Sequence queries are particularly problematic, because their result does not depend on a single record, but by the correlation of multiple records, so the result of a query can be slightly incorrect in case of partial shards (consider the case where a missing event clause matches records that are in missing shards, it will return false positives).
For this reason, we also provide an additional parameter, `allow_partial_sequence_results` to fine-tune the behavior of sequence queries:
- `allow_partial_sequence_results=false` (default): in case of missing shards, sequence queries always return empty results, to avoid mistakes
- `allow_partial_sequence_results=true`: the sequences are calculated only on the available data, ie. on records present in available shards.

If `allow_partial_search_results=false` (default), then `allow_partial_sequence_results` has no effect.

TODO:
- [x] Implement request parameter and query logic
- [x] Implement response (`shard_failures`)
- [x] Allow override for the default value (eg. with something similar to `search.default_allow_partial_results`)
- [x] Docs
pr_title: EQL: add support for partial shard results
pr_comment: Hi @luigidellaquila, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
merge conflict between base and head
@yctercero if you have a chance, please have a look at this PR, it practically contains the logic we discussed off-line

I think this aligns with what we discussed. Where we'll be able to return partial results for non-sequence EQL queries and disallow partial results for sequence queries. 

I think @marshallmain is out this week, but maybe @approksiu @MikePaquette can confirm this is the desired behavior? Note that users will be allowed to return partial results for sequence queries if they turn on the flag.

> Note that users will be allowed to return partial results for sequence queries if they turn on the flag.

To clarify, partial results for sequences means _full sequences_, but calculated only on the available data (ie. not pieces of sequences / sequences with a smaller number of events)

Hi all, I have a question, if it would be possible to know if the results are based on full or partial available data? 
I want to know in case of setting allow_partial_search_results=true what kind of results were returned to determine if it makes sense to re-run the rule to get complete results.

@approksiu with current implementation, in case of shard failures you'll have an additional `"shard_failures": [...]` in the response. If it's present, you can assume the results are from partial available data.

Thanks! Sounds good to me!
The "shard_failures": [...] message would be present irregardless of a setting I assume?

> The "shard_failures": [...] message would be present irregardless of a setting I assume?

It will always be present in case of shard failures, when `allow_partial_search_results=true`

> It will always be present in case of shard failures, when `allow_partial_search_results=true`

Thanks @luigidellaquila. Is my understanding correct that if `allow_partial_search_results=false`, the "shard_failures": [...] message would not be present?

> Thanks @luigidellaquila. Is my understanding correct that if allow_partial_search_results=false, the "shard_failures": [...] message would not be present?

If `allow_partial_search_results=false` (that is the default) the behavior will be exactly as it is today, ie. if there are no shard failures you get the normal result; if there are shard failures you get an error.

Thanks for your comments folks, I think I addressed all your observations. Please let me know if you have further concerns.

@astefan with my latest commit I added support for partial results also in TOML tests, it should give us a bit more flexibility, and it also covers scenarios with security enabled.

@yctercero @approksiu thanks for the off-line conversations and for confirming that the PR covers your needs.

@astefan @javanna please let me know if you have further remarks of if we can proceed.

review_comment: What happens if an user provides only `allow_partial_sequece_results=true` or uses `allow_partial_search_results=false` and `allow_partial_sequece_results=true` at the same time?

`allow_partial_sequece_results` alone (or with  `allow_partial_search_results=false`) has no effect.
There are randomized tests for this in [PartialSearchResultsIT](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/116388/files#diff-394483381f9a9290704dec509e32ba564499cf341a3b0ee536f7463537137aebR210) , but probably I can extend them a bit, randomly setting `allow_partial_search_results=false`

It would be great if all the existent tests in EQL that have no idea about partial results (all the tests based on BaseEqlSpecTestCase before this PR) would completely randomize these two new settings. All of them should behave completely the same because we have no "broken" shard setup for them which means that irrespective of the values provided, the tests should pass.
There is some randomization already, but I'm making it more complete.
Do we need a setting to tweak the default given it's a flag exposed at the request level?

I'm not completely sure tbh (maybe @yctercero has opinions here).
My thinking is that it could make our life easier on existing deployments, where we have hundreds of EQL rules already configured and we don't want to change them one by one, but maybe this can be addressed at higher level (in Kibana?).

Yes, all the defaults are to `false` now.
The discussion here was more about the real need for a cluster setting to change these defaults, since we can always set these values per query.

I'm with @javanna here. If there is no need for this, let's not make it more complicated than it should be. If there will be a desire in the future for this, we can add it.

The basic principle of **"it's easy to put stuff in, harder to take it out"** (think about BWC) applies here.

Same principle for having this as both **request parameter** and **request body parameter**: it complicates the logic unnecessarily and confuses users with a lot of options to think and reason about. I realize that ES query DSL has this in the same way (both **request parameter** and **request body parameter**) and I am not against this that much, but unless there is an actual need and request I wouldn't confuse users.

@yctercero I remember we discussed this off-line as an option, but I'm not sure if you are actually planning to use these two cluster settings.
Should we keep them?

Let's go with the less complicated option where we would handle it on the Kibana side - say an advanced setting or something of the like. 

cc @approksiu

`allowPartialResultsInBody` value seems to suggest that "partial results" settings can be used **either** as request parameter or request body parameter. I think we should test the case when the user provides:
- request parameter values AND request body parameters (both of them or just one)
- either one of them

In other words, randomize any combination of request parameters presence and values in the two places where we allow them.
